text.en: NUMERICAL METHODS ATLAS · PROBLEM H₂ molecular RHF: independent reference, SCF and s-basis refinement Explore this problem’s equations, reference conditions, methods and published code. Saved result figure Fixed-input H₂ RHF: separate geometry, s-basis sequence and SCF-tolerance comparisons. Reading states PySCF differences, histories and remaining finite-basis limits. Equations and problem definitions Representative equations related to this problem. See the image/problem conditions and each execution example for initial conditions, boundary conditions and parameters. Closed-shell Hartree–Fock equations F^=h^+∑j∈occ(2J^j−K^j),F^ϕi=εiϕi FC=SCε,C†SC=I Closed-shell occupied-orbital RHF equations include nonlocal exchange. Preserve existing He local-reduction and H2RHF examples. New calculations cover only fixed minimal two-electron H2/H3+ models; UHF equations have their own mapped model. No general multicenter molecules, global open-shell stability, complete-basis or general correlated-method guarantee. Stationary electronic Schrödinger equation H^elΨ=EelΨ,Etot=Eel+∑A<BZAZBRAB Fixed-nuclei nonrelativistic electronic eigenproblems; add nuclear repulsion separately. Preserve the existing hydrogenic radial examples. Additional examples are restricted to one-dimensional box/HO and two-electron FCI in at most3AOs, not general many-electron direct solvers or continuum-exact molecules. Unrestricted HF in a minimal two-electron model Fσ=h+J[Pα+Pβ]−K[Pσ],FσCσ=SCσεσ ⟨S2⟩1α,1β=1−∣cα†Scβ∣2 Only2fixed distances. Finite-basis FCI is not continuum exactness, and UHF stationarity is not a general global-minimum guarantee. Angular/complete-basis convergence and a broad dissociation curve remain untested. Formulations used by execution examples Common execution exampleApproximation or discretization H₂ molecular RHF: independent reference, SCF and s-basis refinement F(P)C=SCε,P=2CoCoT ERHF=12Tr⁡[P(h+F)]+1/R Isolated two-electron RHF in finite s-Gaussian bases. Numerical convergence differs from RHF model error. Supplementary execution exampleExample definition or validation formula Minimal-basis H2: RHF, broken-spin UHF and finite-basis FCI Fσ=h+J[Pα+Pβ]−K[Pσ],FσCσ=SCσεσ ⟨S2⟩1α,1β=1−∣cα†Scβ∣2 Hpq,rs=hprδqs+hqsδpr+(pr∣qs),Etot=Eel+ENN Compare RHF, broken-spin UHF and finite-basis FCI for H2 at two fixed geometries in the same minimal basis. Exact and reference solutions Use independent RHF references and SCF/s-type-basis checks for a small fixed H₂ model. Agreement in finite-basis RHF is not agreement with a fully correlated exact molecular solution. Semi-analytic referenceReference for the same problem Minimal-basis H2: RHF, broken-spin UHF and finite-basis FCI F^\sigma=h+J[P^\alpha+P^\beta]-K[P^\sigma],\quad F^\sigma C^\sigma=SC^\sigma\varepsilon^\sigma;\quad \langle S^2\rangle_{1\alpha,1\beta}=1-|c_\alpha^\dagger S c_\beta|^2;\quad H_{pq,rs}=h_{pr}\delta_{qs}+h_{qs}\delta_{pr}+(pr|qs),\quad E_{\rm tot}=E_{\rm el}+E_{NN} Explicit unchanged STO-3G s contraction, R1.4/3.0bohr, finite-basis FCI and broken-spin UHF; not exact continuum chemistry. Distances1.4/3.0bohr and total energies in hartree. Two electrons in2AOs, each an explicitly supplied three-primitive contracted Hs function. Only2fixed distances. Finite-basis FCI is not continuum exactness, and UHF stationarity is not a general global-minimum guarantee. Angular/complete-basis convergence and a broad dissociation curve remain untested. References and results of execution examples Common execution example H₂ molecular RHF: independent reference, SCF and s-basis refinement Independent PySCF imports no educational solver. Same-geometry, same-finite-basis RHF, not an exact correlated solution. Independent PySCF imports no educational solver. Same-geometry, same-finite-basis RHF, not an exact correlated solution. Compare STO-3G and nested s-Gaussian spaces at three separations. Numerical RHF validation, not molecular DFT, periodic, complete-basis or correct-dissociation validation. Conditions, commands and validation scope Assumptions Fixed nuclei, singlet restricted HF, one doubly occupied spatial orbital.
